answer.generated:
To retrieve the first name, last name, and royalty amount of authors who have written titles, along with those authors who have not written any titles but should still appear in the result set with NULL values for the royalty amount, a left outer join can be utilized. The query should start by selecting the relevant columns from the authors and titleauthor tables, ensuring that all authors from the authors table are included in the result set, even if they do not have a corresponding entry in the titleauthor table. This is achieved through a left outer join on the authors.a_u_id and titleauthor.au_id columns. The full SQL query would look as follows:

```sql
SELECT authors.a_u_fname, authors.a_u_lname, titleauthor.royalty
FROM authors
LEFT OUTER JOIN titleauthor
ON authors.a_u_id = titleauthor.au_id;
```

This query ensures that all authors are included in the result set, and for those authors without any associated titles, the royalty column will display NULL values. The left outer join operation effectively matches authors to their titles, while also retaining all authors from the authors table, thus fulfilling the requirement of including authors who have not written any titles.
